recipes.name: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
ingredients: 1 medium (~ 8 oz / 227g) pear, (peeled and cut into ¼” pieces (a fine dice) (see Note 1))
1 tablespoon (7g) freshly grated ginger ((use 2 tsp for a milder flavor))
1 cinnamon stick ((or ½ tsp ground cinnamon))
Scant ⅔ cup (135g) organic cane sugar ((see Note 2))
instructions: Measure out ⅓ cup (35g) of the cranberries and set aside for the end.
Zest an orange to yield 2 teaspoons; set aside for the end. Juice the oranges to yield ¾ cup (180 mL) juice.

In a medium (3-quart / 3L) saucepan, combine the remaining cranberries, orange juice (but not zest), the pear, ginger, nutmeg, cinnamon stick, the sugar, 2 pinches of kosher salt (or 1 pinch sea salt), and 2 tablespoons (30 mL) filtered water.

Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to medium and stir occasionally until the cranberries break down and are popping, 4 to 5 minutes.Use the back of a wooden spoon to press the cranberries against the side of the pot and cook for another 3 minutes or until thickened (if it's bubbling very vigorously, reduce the heat a touch).Add the orange zest and reserved cranberries and cook over medium-low heat for 1 to 2 more minutes, or until you have a jam-like consistency.

Remove from the heat and discard the cinnamon stick. Cool for 20 minutes or until room temp. NOTE: the sauce will be quite thick, which is my preference, but if you want a looser consistency, return to the saucepan with a few splashes of water and simmer until well incorporated.

page_recipe_notes: Notes I love the sweetness and texture of a pear, but if you don’t have pears, you could also use a medium-sized tart-sweet apple. This cranberry sauce is designed to be sweet but not too sweet and perfectly tart. If it ends up too tart for your taste, you can always add a bit more sugar, a splash of water, and simmer again. I don’t recommend reducing the sugar though—in my experience, the sauce turned out too sour and even a little bitter.
